content.text: Case Study – Real Estate Transactions and Title Deeds
challenges in translating real estate contracts and ownership documents

Key legal concepts in real estate transactions
The structure and function of title deeds
Common clauses in real estate contracts and sales agreements

A. Overview: Why Real Estate Law Matters
ownership, sale, and transfer of property
is the legal document that proves ownership and records rights over land or real estate.
Property ownership must be clearly defined
Real estate contracts must include key clauses
related to payment, transfer, and legal obligations.
Ambiguous translations can affect legal validity
A buyer may challenge a property sale if the title is unclear.
An improperly translated real estate contract may create enforceability issues.
Failure to translate encumbrances correctly may cause financial or legal problems for the new owner.
"What legal protections ensure that a property transaction is valid?"
"How does a title deed differ from a real estate contract?"
"What challenges arise when translating real estate contracts across jurisdictions?"
2. Key Legal Terms in Real Estate Law
A legal document proving ownership of property
"The buyer received the title deed after completing the purchase."
A claim or restriction on a property’s use
"The mortgage is an encumbrance that must be cleared before sale."
A legal right over a property used as security for a debt
"The lender placed a lien on the property until the loan was repaid."
A loan secured by real estate
"The homeowner obtained a mortgage to finance the purchase."
A legal right to use another person's land for a specific purpose
"The utility company has an easement to install power lines."
A deed that transfers property without guaranteeing clear title
"The seller transferred the property using a quitclaim deed."
ownership rights, financial obligations, or land use restrictions
B. Common Clauses in Real Estate Contracts
Provides a legal description of the property
"The property is legally described as Lot 12, Block 5 of Springfield Estates."
States the agreed-upon price and payment terms
"The buyer agrees to pay $500,000 for the property in installments."
Confirms the seller’s right to transfer ownership
"The seller warrants that they hold clear title to the property."
Declares any existing liens, mortgages, or legal restrictions
"The property is subject to an existing mortgage of $200,000."
Defines the date and conditions for finalizing the sale
"The closing shall take place on July 1, 2024, at which time title shall transfer to the buyer."
its function in ensuring a valid property transaction
3. Challenges in Translating Real Estate Legal Documents
Real estate laws differ across jurisdictions
Certain property law terms have no direct equivalents
Ambiguity in translation may cause title disputes and legal conflicts.
Título de propriedade com garantia de titularidade
Conta fiduciária para depósito de valores antes do fechamento do contrato
Restrição legal ou financeira sobre um imóvel
B. Avoiding Ambiguity in Real Estate Translation
Unclear property descriptions may create ownership disputes.
Poor translation of legal restrictions may result in financial liabilities.
Failure to properly adapt contract terms may affect enforceability.
Identify potential translation issues in this sentence:
"The buyer agrees to purchase the property subject to all existing encumbrances and restrictions of record."
4. Reading Practice: Real Estate Legal Documents
Read the following excerpts aloud and analyze key legal terms.

"This deed, made this 5th day of May 2024, between John Doe, the Grantor, and Jane Smith, the Grantee, conveys all rights, title, and interest in the real property described as follows: Lot 15, Block 7 of Pinewood Estates. The Grantor warrants that the property is free from liens and encumbrances, except as noted herein."
is being used in this transfer?
does the grantor provide to the grantee?
translate this document while maintaining legal clarity

"The Seller agrees to transfer the Property to the Buyer for the total purchase price of $750,000. The parties agree that the sale shall close on August 15, 2024, at which time the Seller shall execute and deliver a Warranty Deed transferring title. The Buyer acknowledges that the property is being sold ‘as-is’ with no further warranties except as expressly stated herein."
5. Writing Exercise: Drafting a Real Estate Clause
using at least three legal terms from today’s lesson.

"The Seller agrees to convey the Property to the Buyer via a Warranty Deed, free of all liens and encumbrances, except as stated herein. The total purchase price of $500,000 shall be paid in full at closing, which shall take place no later than December 1, 2024. The Buyer acknowledges that the Property is transferred in its current condition, subject to all zoning regulations and easements of record."
